record.paper_title: Minimal positive realizations: a survey of recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Given a positive realization of a transfer function, how can one approximate it by another positive realization of lower state dimension while preserving positivity?

evidence.quote: - how can one approximate a positive realization by a lower dimension one?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H(z)$ be a rational transfer function of a discrete-time single-input single-output linear system, and suppose $(A,b,c)$ is a positive realization of $H$, i.e. matrices $A\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{n\times n}$, $b\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{n\times 1}$, $c\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{1\times n}$ with nonnegative entries such that
$$H(z) = c(zI - A)^{-1}b.$$
Given such a positive realization $(A,b,c)$ of state dimension $n$ and a target dimension $m < n$, develop a constructive procedure that produces a positive realization $(\tilde A, \tilde b, \tilde c)$ of state dimension $m$, with $\tilde A\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{m\times m}$, $\tilde b\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{m\times 1}$, $\tilde c\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{1\times m}$, whose associated transfer function $\tilde H(z) = \tilde c(zI - \tilde A)^{-1}\tilde b$ approximates $H(z)$ in a prescribed system norm (e.g. $H^\infty$ or $H^2$). In particular, characterize when such a lower-dimensional positive approximation exists, quantify the achievable approximation error as a function of $m$, and give an algorithm that, while strictly preserving entrywise nonnegativity of all the matrices involved, computes a best (or near-best) positive approximant of dimension $m$.
artifact.status_search_result: The minimal positive realization problem itself remains open in general (only upper and lower bounds on the minimal dimension are known), and the corresponding model-reduction question of approximating a positive realization by one of lower state dimension while preserving nonnegativity is an active research topic without a general solution. Recent work (e.g. on minimal positive Markov realizations, 2025) continues to provide only partial results and bounds.

status_evidence.title: A Tutorial on the Positive Realization Problem
status_evidence.snippet: it is not known, to date, how to determine in general the minimum dimension of a positive realization and only lower and upper bounds to it are available.
status_evidence.claim: Determining the minimal positive realization dimension is still open in general.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive Markov realizations (arXiv 2502.21102)
status_evidence.snippet: A linear programming approach computes positive realizations in Markov form with a minimum dimension, providing an upper bound on the minimal positive realization dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work (2025) still only provides bounds and partial solutions related to minimal positive realizations.

status_evidence.title: An upper bound on the dimension of minimal positive realizations for discrete time systems
status_evidence.snippet: Upper bound on the dimension of minimal positive realizations for discrete time systems.
status_evidence.claim: Only bounds, not exact minimal dimensions or approximation procedures, are available.
